endpoints.summary: Entry point for WebGoat, redirects to the first lesson found within the course.
endpoints.description: Entry point for WebGoat, redirects to the first lesson found within the course.

endpoints.summary: Entry point for WebGoat, redirects to the first lesson found within the course.
endpoints.description: Entry point for WebGoat, redirects to the first lesson found within the course.
Redirects the client to the WebWolf application home page using the configured webwolf.url property.
Handles GET requests to paths ending with '.lesson', extracts the lesson name from the URL, and returns a ModelAndView for the lesson content.
Sets the 'welcomed' session attribute if not already set, then forwards the request to /attack?start=true, skipping the welcome page.
Endpoint which generates the report card for the current user to show the stats on the solved lessons.
Returns the value of the 'webgoat.server.directory' property from the application environment.
Returns a list of all hints for the current lesson as JSON.
Checks if debugging of labels is enabled or disabled and returns the current status as JSON.
Returns a map of all the labels from messages and plugin messages as JSON.
Returns the LessonInfoModel for the given lesson name, containing the lesson title and flags indicating whether source, solution, and plan are available.

endpoints.summary: Returns the lesson menu used to build the left navigation.
endpoints.description: Returns a list of LessonMenuItem objects representing categories and lessons, filtered by excludeCategories and excludeLessons, and annotated with completion status from the user's progress.

Endpoint for fetching the complete lesson overview which informs the user about whether all the assignments are solved. Used as the last page of the lesson to generate a lesson overview. Returns a list of assignments with their solved status.

endpoints.summary: Restart a lesson for the current user
endpoints.description: Resets the user's progress for the specified lesson, cleans and migrates the lesson database schema, and re-initializes all initializable lessons for the user.
Endpoint mapped via @RequestMapping without an explicit HTTP method; it accepts GET requests. Currently disabled and returns the message 'Not working...'.
Displays the registration form for creating a new user account.
Validates the submitted user form, creates a new user account, logs the user in, and redirects to the attack page.
Registers an OAuth-authenticated user in the database with a random password and redirects to the welcome page.

Returns a list of rankings for all users (excluding those with usernames starting with 'csrf-'), sorted by the number of challenges solved in descending order. Each ranking includes the username and a list of solved challenge titles.

Verifies the user's account by checking submitted security question answers. If the user likely cheated, returns a failure with a cheating feedback message. Otherwise, if the account verification succeeds, stores the verified user ID in the session and returns success; otherwise returns failure.

Handles POST requests to /BypassRestrictions/FieldRestrictions. Accepts parameters select, radio, checkbox, shortInput, and readOnlyInput. Returns a failed AttackResult if select is 'option1' or 'option2', if radio is 'option1' or 'option2', if checkbox is 'on' or 'off', if shortInput length is <= 5, or if readOnlyInput equals 'change'. Otherwise returns a successful AttackResult.

Handles the BypassRestrictions frontend validation assignment. Accepts seven string fields and an integer error parameter. Returns failure if error > 0 or if any field matches its corresponding regex (indicating the client-side validation was not bypassed). Returns success only when all fields fail to match their regexes, meaning the frontend validation was bypassed.

endpoints.summary: Submit a flag for a challenge
endpoints.description: Accepts a flag number as a path variable and a flag value as a request parameter, then checks whether the submitted flag matches the expected flag for that challenge. Returns a success AttackResult if correct, otherwise a failed AttackResult.
Accepts username and password parameters. The password must be 'admin' and match the PINCODE-derived password. Returns success with flag if correct, otherwise failure.

endpoints.summary: Returns the WebGoat logo image with an embedded pincode
endpoints.description: Handles GET requests to /challenge/logo, reads the webgoat2.png image from the classpath, embeds the 4-digit PINCODE into specific byte positions (81216-81219), and returns the modified PNG image.

endpoints.summary: Returns the WebGoat logo image with an embedded pincode
endpoints.description: Handles POST requests to /challenge/logo, reads the webgoat2.png image from the classpath, embeds the 4-digit PINCODE into specific byte positions (81216-81219), and returns the modified PNG image.

Authenticates a user for challenge 5. Requires non-empty username_login and password_login parameters. Only accepts username 'Larry'. Constructs a SQL query by concatenating user input directly into the query string, making it vulnerable to SQL injection. If the query returns a result, the challenge is solved and the flag is returned; otherwise, a failure message is returned.
Accepts a password reset link and if it matches the admin password reset link, returns a success message with the flag; otherwise returns 418 I'm a teapot.
Accepts an email address, extracts the username, generates a password reset link, and sends it via email through WebWolf.
Returns a zip file containing the git repository for challenge 7.

Simple implementation of VERB Based Authentication. If the request method is GET, returns an error message indicating login is required. Otherwise, increments the vote count for the given star rating and returns a response with an X-FlagController header containing the flag.
Returns a map of star ratings to their vote counts.
Calculates and returns the average star rating based on all votes.
Throws an IllegalStateException; should never be called.

endpoints.summary: Validate success message for Chrome DevTools lesson
endpoints.description: Accepts a successMessage request parameter and compares it to the value stored in the lesson session under 'randValue'. If they match, returns a success AttackResult with feedback 'xss-dom-message-success'; otherwise returns a failed AttackResult with feedback 'xss-dom-message-failure'.

endpoints.summary: Complete the Chrome DevTools network assignment
endpoints.description: Compares the network_num and number request parameters; returns success if they match, otherwise failure.
Accepts four quiz answers as request parameters, compares each against the predefined solutions, and returns a success or failure AttackResult.
Returns a boolean array indicating which quiz questions were answered correctly in the last submission.

endpoints.summary: Submit answer for Client-Side Filtering assignment
endpoints.description: Accepts a request parameter 'answer' and checks whether it equals '450000'. Returns a success AttackResult with feedback 'assignment.solved' if correct, otherwise a failed AttackResult with feedback 'ClientSideFiltering.incorrect'.

endpoints.summary: Submit a checkout code to complete the Client Side Filtering (free) assignment
endpoints.description: Accepts a checkoutCode request parameter. If the code equals the hardcoded SUPER_COUPON_CODE ('get_it_for_free'), returns a successful AttackResult; otherwise returns a failed AttackResult.

Reads employees.xml from the WebGoat home directory, evaluates an XPath expression to extract UserID, FirstName, LastName, SSN, and Salary for each employee, and returns the results as a JSON list of maps.
Returns the checkout code and discount for the given coupon code. If the code matches the super coupon code, returns a 100% discount code.
Returns all available checkout codes including the super coupon code with 100% discount.

Returns the Basic Authorization header value for the current user. If no basicAuth value is stored in the session, a random secret from HashingAssignment.SECRETS is chosen as the password, the Basic auth string is generated via Base64 encoding of 'username:password', stored in the session, and returned as 'Authorization: Basic <value>'.
Validates the submitted username and password by comparing the Base64-encoded 'username:password' against the basicAuth value stored in the session. Returns success if they match, otherwise failure.

endpoints.summary: Get MD5 hash of a secret
endpoints.description: Returns the MD5 hash of a randomly selected secret from a predefined list. The secret is stored in the session for later verification.

endpoints.summary: Get SHA-256 hash of a secret
endpoints.description: Returns the SHA-256 hash of a randomly selected secret from a predefined list. The secret is stored in the session for later verification.
Accepts two password answers, compares them with the secrets stored in the session, and returns an AttackResult indicating success, partial success, or failure.
Checks if the provided secret file name is 'default_secret' and the SHA-256 hash of the provided secret text matches the expected hash. Returns success or failure feedback accordingly.

endpoints.summary: Get the RSA private key in PEM format
endpoints.description: Returns the private key stored in the session, generating a new RSA key pair if none exists. The private key is returned in PEM format.

endpoints.summary: Verify a signature against the modulus
endpoints.description: Validates that the provided modulus matches the public key's modulus and verifies the signature over the modulus using the public key. Returns success if both checks pass.
Handles the XOR encoding assignment. Accepts a request parameter 'answer_pwd1' and checks if it equals 'databasepassword'. Returns a success AttackResult if correct, otherwise a failed AttackResult.

Confirms the CSRF flag value by comparing the provided confirmFlagVal with the value stored in the lesson session under the key 'csrf-get-success'. Returns a success AttackResult with feedback and output if the values match, otherwise returns a failed AttackResult.

Accepts a plain text feedback body, validates CSRF conditions (JSESSIONID cookie present, Content-Type text/plain, and Referer/Host mismatch), and returns a success flag if the CSRF attack is correctly performed.
Accepts a confirmFlagVal request parameter and compares it with the stored CSRF feedback flag in the lesson session to determine if the assignment is solved.

Handles POST requests to /csrf/basic-get-flag. Reads the 'host' and 'referer' headers and the 'csrf' parameter. If the referer header is missing (NULL), it returns a success response with a random flag, using the 'csrf-get-null-referer.success' message when the csrf parameter equals 'true', otherwise the 'csrf-get-other-referer.success' message. If the referer's host matches the request host, it returns success=false with the message 'Appears the request came from the original host' and a null flag. Otherwise, it returns a success response with a random flag and the 'csrf-get-other-referer.success' message.

Handles POST requests to /csrf/login. Uses the @CurrentUsername annotation to inject the current authenticated user's username. If the username starts with "csrf", returns a successful AttackResult with feedback "csrf-login-success"; otherwise returns a failed AttackResult with feedback "csrf-login-failed" and the username as a feedback argument.
Returns a collection of reviews for the current user combined with predefined reviews.
Creates a new review with the provided text, stars, and validation token. Checks for CSRF token and referer header.

Accepts a Base64-encoded serialized token, decodes it, and deserializes it via ObjectInputStream. If the deserialized object is a VulnerableTaskHolder whose readObject executes a task action (sleep/ping) taking between 3 and 7 seconds, the assignment is marked as solved. Returns failure feedback for wrong object types, invalid versions, or expired objects.

endpoints.summary: Login endpoint for the HijackSession assignment
endpoints.description: Authenticates a user via username/password or an existing hijack_cookie session ID. If no cookie is present, authenticates with credentials and sets a new hijack_cookie. If a cookie is present, authenticates using the cookie value as the session ID. Returns success if authenticated, otherwise failure.

Handles the HTML tampering task by accepting QTY and Total request parameters. It checks whether the quantity multiplied by the price (2999.99) exceeds the provided total by more than 1, returning a success result if the client-side price was tampered with, otherwise a failure result.

endpoints.summary: Submit the HTTP Basics attack1 assignment
endpoints.description: Accepts a 'person' request parameter. If the person value is not blank, returns a success AttackResult with the reversed person string as feedback; otherwise returns a failed AttackResult with an empty feedback message.

Handles POST requests to /HttpBasics/attack2. Accepts request parameters 'answer', 'magic_answer', and 'magic_num'. Returns success if 'answer' equals 'POST' (case-insensitive) and 'magic_answer' equals 'magic_num'; otherwise returns a failure result with appropriate feedback.
Handles POST requests to /HttpProxies/intercept-request. POST requests always fail with feedback 'http-proxies.intercept.failure'.

Handles GET requests to /HttpProxies/intercept-request. Succeeds if header 'x-request-intercepted' is true and parameter 'changeMe' equals 'Requests are tampered easily' (case-insensitive); otherwise fails.

endpoints.summary: Submit attributes for IDOR diff-attributes assignment
endpoints.description: Accepts a comma-separated list of attributes and checks whether the combination includes 'userid' and 'role' to determine if the IDOR diff-attributes assignment is solved.

Accepts a user ID path variable and a JSON body containing a UserProfile. It retrieves the authenticated user ID from the session, then checks if the submitted profile's userId differs from the authenticated user ID. If so, it updates the profile with the submitted color and role, stores it in the session, and returns success or failure based on the role and color values. This endpoint demonstrates an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability because it does not properly verify that the authenticated user is authorized to edit the specified profile.

Authenticates a user for the IDOR lesson. Only the user 'tom' with password 'cat' is allowed to log in successfully; other users or incorrect passwords result in failure. On success, stores the authenticated username and user ID in the lesson session.

endpoints.summary: View another user's profile by ID
endpoints.description: Retrieves the profile of a user specified by the userId path variable. The endpoint checks that the session is authenticated as 'tom' and that the requested userId differs from the authenticated user's ID. It then returns the profile if the userId corresponds to '2342388', otherwise returns a failure message.
Returns the profile details of the authenticated user if authenticated as 'tom'.
Returns the profile details of the authenticated user if authenticated as 'tom'.

endpoints.summary: View own profile via alternate URL path
endpoints.description: Handles POST requests to /IDOR/profile/alt-path. Accepts a 'url' request parameter and checks if the authenticated user is 'tom'. If so, it parses the URL to verify it matches the pattern WebGoat/IDOR/profile/{authUserId} and returns the user's profile information. Otherwise, it returns a failure message.
Accepts username and password request parameters. If username equals 'CaptainJack' and password equals 'BlackPearl', returns a successful AttackResult; otherwise returns a failed AttackResult.
Empty endpoint that exists only so the client-side JavaScript can call an existing endpoint. Returns HTTP 202 Accepted.
Handles POST requests to /JWT/decode. Accepts the request parameter 'jwt-encode-user' and returns a success AttackResult if the value equals 'user', otherwise a failed AttackResult.
Accepts two quiz answers as request parameters and checks if they contain the correct solutions. Returns success if both answers are correct, otherwise failure.
Returns an array of booleans indicating which quiz questions were answered correctly in the last submission.

endpoints.summary: Login endpoint for JWT refresh lesson
endpoints.description: Accepts JSON with user and password. If user is Jerry and password matches PASSWORD, returns new access and refresh tokens.

endpoints.summary: Checkout endpoint for JWT refresh lesson
endpoints.description: Validates JWT from Authorization header. If user is Tom, returns success; if alg is none, returns specific feedback. Otherwise returns failure.

endpoints.summary: Refresh token endpoint for JWT refresh lesson
endpoints.description: Validates JWT and refresh token. If refresh token is valid, issues new tokens and invalidates the old refresh token.

endpoints.summary: Generate a JWT token signed with a secret key
endpoints.description: Returns a JWT token built with issuer 'WebGoat Token Builder', audience 'webgoat.org', issued at current time, expiring in 60 seconds, subject 'tom@webgoat.org', and claims username=Tom, Email=tom@webgoat.org, Role=[Manager, Project Administrator]. The token is signed using HS256 with a randomly selected secret from a predefined list.

endpoints.summary: Validate a JWT token for the JWT secret key lesson
endpoints.description: Parses the provided JWT token using the secret key. Checks that the token contains all expected claims (iss, iat, exp, aud, sub, username, Email, Role). If the username claim equals 'WebGoat' (case-insensitive), the lesson is marked as solved; otherwise, it returns a failure with feedback. If parsing fails, returns an invalid token error.

Authenticates a user by checking if the provided username is in the valid users list. If valid, it creates a JWT token with admin=false and the username, sets it as a cookie named 'access_token', and returns HTTP 200. If invalid, it clears the cookie and returns HTTP 401.

Returns a list of votes sorted by average rating in descending order. The response is serialized using Jackson views: if no valid access token is provided or the user is not valid, the GuestView is used; otherwise, the UserView is used, which includes additional fields like numberOfVotes, votingAllowed, and average.

endpoints.summary: Cast a vote for a specific title
endpoints.description: Increments the number of votes for the vote with the given title. Requires a valid JWT access token with a valid user. If the token is missing or invalid, returns HTTP 401. If the user is not valid, returns HTTP 401. If successful, returns HTTP 202 Accepted.

Resets all votes to their initial state. Requires a valid JWT access token with admin claim set to true. If the token is missing or invalid, returns a failure message. If the user is not admin, returns a failure message indicating admin only. If successful, resets all votes and returns success.
Follows the specified user. If the user is 'Jerry', returns a message indicating following yourself is redundant; otherwise returns a message that you are now following Tom.

Verifies a JWT token using the JKU header to fetch the public key, then checks the username claim. If the username is 'Jerry', returns a failure; if 'Tom', returns success; otherwise returns a failure indicating the user is not Tom.
Follows the specified user. If the user is 'Jerry', returns a message that following yourself is redundant; otherwise returns that you are now following Tom.

Parses the provided JWT token using a signing key resolver that looks up the key by the 'kid' header from the database. If the token is valid and the username claim is 'Tom', the assignment is marked as solved. If the username is 'Jerry', it fails with a specific feedback. Otherwise, it fails with a different feedback.
Handles POST requests to /lesson-template/sample-attack. Checks if param1 equals the secret value 'secr37Value' and returns success or failure accordingly.
Returns a list of items in the basket for the specified user.

Accepts username and password parameters. Returns success if username is 'Admin' and password matches the randomly generated password logged at startup; otherwise returns failure. Empty username or password results in a failure with an output message.

Handles the LogSpoofing lesson assignment. Accepts username and password request parameters. If username is empty, returns a failed result. Otherwise replaces newline characters with
and rejects usernames containing

or

. Returns success if the
tag appears before the string 'admin' in the username, otherwise returns failure.

endpoints.summary: Submit hidden menu selections for the Missing Function Access Control hidden menus lesson
endpoints.description: Accepts two hidden menu values (hiddenMenu1 and hiddenMenu2). Returns success if hiddenMenu1 is 'Users' and hiddenMenu2 is 'Config'; returns a 'close' failure if hiddenMenu1 is 'Config' and hiddenMenu2 is 'Users'; otherwise returns a generic failure. Produces application/json.
Returns a ModelAndView rendering the list_users view with all users and their display representations.
Returns a JSON list of DisplayUser objects for all users using the admin password salt, but only if the current user is an admin; otherwise returns 403 Forbidden.
Accepts a JSON User object and saves it to the repository, returning the saved user. Returns null on error.

endpoints.summary: Add a new user (admin fix path)
endpoints.description: Accepts a JSON User object and saves it to the repository, returning the saved user. Returns null on error.

endpoints.summary: Submit a user hash for the missing function access control lesson
endpoints.description: Accepts a userHash parameter, computes the expected hash for the user 'Jerry' using the simple password salt, and returns success if the supplied hash matches; otherwise returns failure.

Accepts a userHash parameter and compares it against the hash generated for the admin user 'Jerry' using the admin password salt. Returns success if the hash matches, otherwise returns a failure feedback.

Accepts form-encoded parameters 'username' and 'securityQuestion'. Returns failure if username is 'webgoat', failure with unknown-user feedback if the username is not in the known colors map, success if the provided security question answer matches the stored color for the user, otherwise failure.

Handles login attempts for the password reset lesson. If the email matches Tom's email, it checks the provided password against the stored password for the current user. If the password matches the default Tom password, it fails with a specific feedback; if it matches the user's stored password, it succeeds. Otherwise, it fails with a generic feedback.
Displays the password reset form if the provided reset link is valid (exists in the resetLinks list). If the link is invalid, it shows a 'password link not found' page.

Processes the password change form. Validates the password field, checks if the reset link is valid, and if the link belongs to Tom, updates the user's password for Tom. Returns the appropriate view (success, password reset form with errors, or link not found).

endpoints.summary: Send a password reset link to the provided email
endpoints.description: Generates a password reset link (UUID), stores it, and either sends an email to the user or, if the email is Tom's and the Host header points to WebWolf, stores the reset link for the current user and simulates clicking the link.
Accepts a security question as a request parameter, checks if it is a known question, increments the count of tried questions, and returns an AttackResult indicating success or providing feedback.

endpoints.summary: Login with email and password for password reset simple mail assignment
endpoints.description: Handles POST requests to /PasswordReset/simple-mail with form-encoded email and password parameters. Extracts the username from the email and checks if it matches the current WebGoat username and if the reversed username equals the provided password. Returns success if both conditions are met, otherwise returns a failure message.

endpoints.summary: Reset password by sending an email with a new password
endpoints.description: Handles POST requests to /PasswordReset/simple-mail/reset with a form-encoded emailReset parameter. Extracts the username from the email and sends a password reset email containing the reversed username as the new password, provided the username matches the current WebGoat username.
Handles file upload for the PathTraversal lesson. Accepts a multipart file and an optional full name, then delegates to ProfileUploadBase.execute for processing.
Returns the profile picture for the current user as a base64-encoded JPEG image.

endpoints.summary: Upload a profile picture with path traversal fix
endpoints.description: Handles file upload for the path traversal lesson with a fix that removes '../' sequences from the provided full name. Accepts a multipart file and an optional full name, then delegates to the base class for processing.

endpoints.summary: Retrieve the profile picture for the current user
endpoints.description: Returns the profile picture (as base64 encoded JPEG) for the authenticated user in the path traversal lesson.

endpoints.summary: Upload a profile picture file for the path traversal lesson (remove user input variant)
endpoints.description: Handles multipart file uploads for the PathTraversal lesson. The uploaded file is passed to ProfileUploadBase.execute along with its original filename and the current username. The base class writes the file into a per-user upload directory and checks whether a path traversal attempt was made by comparing canonical paths.

endpoints.summary: Submit the secret answer for the path traversal assignment
endpoints.description: Accepts a 'secret' request parameter and the current username. If the SHA-512 hex digest of the username matches the provided secret (case-insensitive), the assignment is marked as solved; otherwise it fails.

endpoints.summary: Retrieve a random cat picture or a specific picture by id
endpoints.description: Returns a cat picture from the cats directory. The 'id' query parameter selects a specific picture; if omitted, a random picture (1-10) is chosen. The query string is validated to reject '..' or '/' characters. If the resolved file is 'path-traversal-secret.jpg', its raw bytes are returned. If the file exists, its Base64-encoded content is returned with a Location header. If not found, a 404 is returned with a list of files in the parent directory.

endpoints.summary: Upload a zip file for the Zip Slip path traversal lesson
endpoints.description: Accepts a multipart zip file upload, validates the file extension, and processes the zip contents to check for path traversal (Zip Slip) vulnerability. Returns an AttackResult indicating whether the lesson was solved.

endpoints.summary: Retrieve the current user's profile picture
endpoints.description: Returns the profile picture for the authenticated user as a JPEG image. Delegates to the parent class implementation.

endpoints.summary: Get profile image for a specific username
endpoints.description: This endpoint always returns a 404 Not Found response. It is likely a placeholder or decoy endpoint.

endpoints.summary: Evaluate password strength for Secure Passwords assignment
endpoints.description: Accepts a password request parameter, measures its strength using zxcvbn, builds an HTML output with length, estimated guesses, score, cracking time, warnings and suggestions, and returns success if the score is 4 or failure otherwise.

Handles login requests. If no spoof_auth cookie is present, performs credential-based login and sets a cookie on success. If the cookie is present, performs cookie-based login. Returns an AttackResult indicating success or failure.
Clears the spoof_auth cookie by setting its max age to 0 and adding it to the response.

endpoints.summary: Register a new user for the SQL injection challenge
endpoints.description: Registers a new user with the provided username, email, and password. The method checks for existing users and inserts a new user if none exists. It is vulnerable to SQL injection as it concatenates user input directly into a SQL query.
Authenticates a user against the sql_challenge_users table using the provided username and password. Returns success only if the username is 'tom' and the credentials match a row in the database.

endpoints.summary: SQL Injection advanced lesson 6a attack endpoint
endpoints.description: Accepts a userid_6a parameter and executes a vulnerable SQL query to demonstrate SQL injection. The query is built by concatenating the user input into a SELECT statement. The endpoint checks if the result contains 'dave' and 'passW0rD' to determine success.

endpoints.summary: Submit user ID for SQL injection advanced lesson 6b
endpoints.description: Accepts a user ID parameter and checks if it matches the password retrieved from the database for user 'dave'. Returns success if matched, otherwise failure.

endpoints.summary: Submit answers for the SQL injection advanced quiz
endpoints.description: Accepts five solution arrays (question_0_solution through question_4_solution), compares the first element of each against the predefined solutions, and returns a success or failure AttackResult. Correct answers are tracked in the guesses array.
Returns a boolean array indicating which quiz questions have been answered correctly.

Handles POST requests to /SqlInjection/attack10 with a required 'action_string' request parameter. It builds a SQL query by concatenating the user-supplied action_string into a LIKE clause (SELECT * FROM access_log WHERE action LIKE '%<action>%') and executes it against the lesson database. The endpoint is vulnerable to SQL injection and is used to test whether the user can drop/remove the access_log table (availability attack). Returns an AttackResult indicating success if the access_log table no longer exists, otherwise failure with the query results or error message.

endpoints.summary: SQL Injection attack endpoint for lesson 2
endpoints.description: Accepts a raw SQL query parameter and executes it against the lesson database. If the first row's department column equals 'Marketing', the assignment is marked as solved and a table of results is returned; otherwise the attempt fails.

Accepts a 'query' request parameter and executes it as an SQL update against the lesson database to complete SQL injection lesson 3. The lesson is completed if the department of Tobi Barnett becomes 'Sales'.
Executes the provided SQL query and checks if the 'phone' column exists in the employees table. Returns success if the column exists, otherwise failure.

Handles POST requests to /SqlInjection/attack5. Accepts a 'query' parameter, creates the unauthorized_user database user, and executes the supplied SQL query via injectableQuery. The lesson is marked complete if the query grants the GRANT_RIGHTS table privilege to UNAUTHORIZED_USER.

Accepts account, operator, and injection parameters, constructs a SQL query by concatenating them, and executes it against the database. Returns an AttackResult indicating success or failure based on the query results.
Handles POST requests to /SqlInjection/assignment5b, taking userid and login_count request parameters and passing them to injectableQuery to perform a SQL query vulnerable to injection.

endpoints.summary: SQL Injection attack endpoint for lesson 8
endpoints.description: Handles POST requests to /SqlInjection/attack8 with parameters 'name' and 'auth_tan'. Constructs a SQL query by concatenating user input, executes it, and returns an AttackResult indicating success or failure based on the number of returned rows.
Handles POST requests to /SqlInjection/attack9 with parameters name and auth_tan, delegating to injectableQueryIntegrity to perform an injectable SQL query that checks salary integrity.
Retrieves a list of servers from the database, sorted by the specified column. The column parameter is directly concatenated into the SQL query, making it vulnerable to SQL injection.

Accepts seven request parameters (field1-field7) and verifies that each contains the expected SQL mitigation-related string in order: getConnection, PreparedStatement, prepareStatement, ?, ?, setString, setString. Returns success if all match, otherwise failure.

endpoints.summary: Submit Java code for SQL injection mitigation lesson 10b
endpoints.description: Accepts an 'editor' request parameter containing Java code. Validates that the code sets up a connection, uses a PreparedStatement with a placeholder, calls setString, and executes the statement. Also compiles the submitted code and returns success if the code is valid and compiles without errors, otherwise returns failure with feedback or compiler errors.

Handles POST requests to /SqlInjectionMitigations/attack12a. Takes an 'ip' request parameter and uses a PreparedStatement to query the 'servers' table for a matching ip and hostname 'webgoat-prd'. Returns success if a record is found, otherwise failure.

endpoints.summary: SQL Injection mitigation with input validation
endpoints.description: Validates that the user ID does not contain spaces, then delegates to SqlInjectionLesson6a.injectableQuery to execute the query. Returns an AttackResult indicating whether the lesson was completed.

endpoints.summary: SQL Injection with keyword-based input validation
endpoints.description: This endpoint attempts to prevent SQL injection by removing the keywords 'FROM' and 'SELECT' (case-insensitive) from the user-supplied 'userid_sql_only_input_validation_on_keywords' parameter. If the resulting string contains a space, the request fails. Otherwise, it delegates to SqlInjectionLesson6a.injectableQuery to execute the query.
Handles POST requests to /SSRF/task1, accepting a 'url' request parameter and returning an AttackResult by calling stealTheCheese(url).

Handles POST requests to /SSRF/task2 with a 'url' request parameter. It checks if the URL matches 'http://ifconfig.pro' and attempts to fetch its content. If successful, returns a success result with the fetched HTML; otherwise returns a failure result.

Accepts a 'payload' request parameter, sanitizes it, and deserializes it using XStream into a Contact object. If the deserialized object is not a ContactImpl, or if an exception is thrown during processing, the assignment is marked as completed. This endpoint is intentionally vulnerable to XStream deserialization attacks (CVE-2013-7285).

endpoints.summary: Submit the unique code for the WebWolf landing assignment
endpoints.description: Accepts a uniqueCode parameter and the current username. If the reversed username equals the uniqueCode, the assignment is marked as solved; otherwise a failure feedback is returned.

endpoints.summary: Open the WebWolf password reset page
endpoints.description: Returns a ModelAndView for the WebWolf password reset page, providing the landing page URL and the reversed username as the unique code.

endpoints.summary: Send a test email via WebWolf
endpoints.description: Sends a test email through WebWolf. The email's local part (before '@') must match the current WebGoat username; otherwise a mismatch message is returned. On success, an Email object is posted to the configured WebWolf mail URL.
Completes the WebWolf introduction assignment by verifying that the provided unique code equals the reverse of the current username. Returns success if correct, otherwise a failure message.

Handles POST requests to complete the Cross-Site Scripting lesson 1 assignment. Accepts an optional 'checkboxAttack1' request parameter; if present, returns a success result, otherwise returns a failure result with feedback.

endpoints.summary: Completes the DOM XSS assignment by validating parameters and header.

It generates a random value, stores it in the lesson session, and checks if param1 equals 42, param2 equals 24, and the 'webgoat-requested-by' header equals 'dom-xss-vuln'. If all conditions are met, it returns a success AttackResult with the random value; otherwise, it returns a failed AttackResult.

Returns a success AttackResult if all checks pass, otherwise a failure result.

Accepts the editor2 request parameter, strips HTML tags, and checks whether the submitted code contains the required AntiSamy-based sanitization pattern (Policy.getInstance("antisamy-slashdot.xml"), new AntiSamy(), .scan(newComment, ...), CleanResults, MyCommentDAO.addComment(threadID, userID, ...getCleanHTML())). Returns a success AttackResult if the pattern matches, otherwise a failure result.

endpoints.summary: Submit a comment for the blind XXE assignment
endpoints.description: Accepts a comment string (XML) and checks if it contains the secret file contents for the user. If so, the assignment is marked as solved. Otherwise, the XML is parsed and the comment is added to the user's comments. This endpoint is vulnerable to blind XXE as the XML parser is configured without disabling external entities.

endpoints.summary: Retrieve comments for the current user
endpoints.description: Returns a collection of comments visible to the authenticated user, including default comments and any user-specific comments.

endpoints.summary: Create a new user comment via JSON or XML
endpoints.description: Accepts a comment string and Content-Type header. If Content-Type is application/json, parses JSON and adds comment. If Content-Type contains application/xml, parses XML (potentially vulnerable to XXE) and checks if the comment text contains certain directory names to mark the assignment as solved.

endpoints.summary: Create a new comment via XML
endpoints.description: Parses the posted XML comment, adds it to the comments cache, and checks whether the XXE solution was achieved by looking for system directory names in the comment text.
